findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: A container of cooked chicken wings and French fries were stored in close proximity of the handwashing sink. Discussed moving the food items to a different location to prevent contamination. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed a leak at the handwashing sink. PIC mentioned that the facility is working to repair the leaking pipe. Ensure that pipes are maintained in good repair and never leaking.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:

The chicken was moved down to a proper storage place in the 2 door cooler and cabbage was moved to the vegetable side in the walk in cooler. Take care to properly protect food in the cold holding units. The violation is considered corrected on site.

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Inspector observed chlorine to be at approximately 10ppm in the sanitizer bucket. The bucket was remade to have 100ppm of chlorine. The violation is considered corrected on site. Take care to change buckets or test them regularly to know when to change them in order to maintain proper sanitizer concentration. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Inspector observed some foods in the top of the make table to be between 47F and 50F. The Unit has been open for the last two hours during lunch and the foods are stacked high in the pans. More than a dozen hot dogs and 12 pizza puffs were discarded. The violation is considered corrected on site. Ensure that the unit is being used in a way that does not allow food temperatures to rise above 41F.

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.comment:

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handlers cards at the facility. PIC could not find the licenses. Discussed keeping a public health folder/binder with all the necessary documentation including food handlers licenses. Ensure new employees have a food handlers card within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no proof of allergen training certification. One CFPM has completed the allergen training certification and it was noted in the last inspection. Ensure the other CFPM takes the allergen training course and both certificates are available at the facility. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.comment:

(C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed raw chicken to be improperly thawing in the 3 compartment sink. No running water was being utilized, though product was submerged in cold water. Discussed proper thawing methods with PIC. PIC was aware of proper thawing methods. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed mop to be stored within the mop bucket and not hanging in a manner that allows to air and/or drip dry. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed CFPM to lack allergen training. Provided paperwork. Discussed need for all CFPM’s to complete allergen training certification and keep proof of licensure on hand at facility. Complete allergen training before the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/12/21.
